body: Trigger: docker is on PATH but its daemon is not running (Docker Desktop installed and stopped, a common macOS state), and the project's runs make no docker object at all, as this project's dashboard drive does. Path: stack down <tag> -> stack:take_down -> stack:removal_steps -> stack:remove_docker -> stack:docker_ids -> stack:docker_out(['ps','-a','-q','--filter','label=ok.run-tag=<tag>']); docker exits 1 with 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon ...', which DOCKER_ABSENT does not match and absent_ok is not set for the list call, so DockerFailed is recorded as a refusal for each of the four DOCKER_STEPS (stack:575-586). Harm: down keeps the entry with four refusals and exits 1 (stack:779-782, 'the run ... is not all taken down'), though the run made nothing docker holds; the run folder is deleted but the entry and its lease stay. stack cleanup then meets the same refusal on every later call: stack:in_use returns 'docker could not list its containers' (stack:796-800), so the entry is left forever and cleanup never takes it down, and every converge drive and confirm round names a failed stack down in its return. The work item says down deletes the entry once every removal succeeds and that a refusal is docker refusing a removal; an unreachable daemon refuses no removal of an object this run made. Scope: caused (new code in scripts/stack).

Trigger: an exception or interrupt (KeyboardInterrupt, a failed registry write, a lock wait interrupted) after stack:spawn_holder returns and before stack:record_holder has written the holder's pid (stack:699-700). Path: stack:start_run except BaseException -> stack:take_down(root, tag, holder) -> stack:claim returns the entry as the registry holds it, holder None -> stack:removal_steps -> stack:stop_group: 'pgid = entry.get("holder"); if pgid is None: return None' (stack:536-538), so the passed child, the holder process, is never signalled or waited. Harm: settle deletes the entry (no refusals), and the holder, 'python -c import signal; signal.pause() ok-stack-hold <tag>', runs forever with no registry entry, so neither down nor cleanup can find it: a process the run made outlives the run with no record, against decision run-artifacts-recorded-by-the-stack-tool ('every process ... belongs to the process group the tool started it in, which down stops'). Scope: caused (new code in scripts/stack).

body: Trigger: a project follows rule 10 and the stack declaration text to write its declared stack.start, e.g. 'docker compose up --build' or a dev server run in the foreground. Path: converge/SKILL.md drive step 2 files the exec task '.ok-planner/bin/stack up' -> scripts/stack::up -> ::start_run, which runs subprocess.run(command, ...) and waits for the start command to exit (scripts/stack:703-705). A start command that keeps the stack in the foreground never exits, so stack up never prints the tag, the exec task never closes, and the drive (and the audit's 'The deployment' step, and every verification path rule 10 step 5 sends through stack up) stalls with no message. Harm: a stall a developer meets by following the suite's own rule text (A3, the drive and stack tool being scripts the project ships). Evidence: the only text that says stack up waits for its command and that a server must be started in the background is review/seed/project.md's 'Resources a driver starts' paragraph, for driver resources alone ('stack up waits for the command to exit, so write the start as one command ... that starts any server in the background'). The texts that teach the declared start command say nothing of it: docs/plumbline-coding.md rule 10 steps 4-6 ('labels every docker container ... leaves no process outside its process group (no setsid, no daemonizing)', which reads as forbidding backgrounding), scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md 'Per-run artifacts and verification stacks' ('runs the declared start command from the project root in a process group of its own'), ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack' ('start is the command that builds and starts the stack'), and stack's USAGE. Scope: caused by the change (stack tool and rule 10 rewrite are new in this sprint).

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack:removal_steps (with ::take_down, ::settle, ::down). removal_steps runs the recorded stop first ('if entry.get("declared") and entry.get("stop"): refusals += attempt_step(tag, "stop", lambda: run_stop(root, tag, entry))', stack:615-616), then remove_folder deletes the run folder whatever the stop returned (stack:622), and settle keeps the entry with refused set because refusals is non-empty (stack:662-667). Trigger: a declared stop command that fails once, where the stop depends on something down has then deleted, such as a compose file under $OK_RUN_FOLDER. Every later 'stack down <tag>' and 'stack cleanup' re-runs the same recorded entry['stop'] against a folder that no longer exists, so it fails every time: the entry, its lease, and its refusal stay for good, the leased ports are never released (repeated failures drain port_range until 'stack up' refuses 'holds too few leasable ports'), and cleanup exits 1 on every later run. down's refusal, 'its entry stays, and stack cleanup tries it again' (stack:780), promises a retry that can never settle it, and no verb or message names a way to drop the entry. Harm (A3): an operator script ends in a state where later use fails. Scope: caused by the change (scripts/stack is new). From report i4.

(2) retired_ports (true-up:372-376) drops every defect starting 'ports' while ports holds the retired object form, so config_offers offers nothing for the collision and draft_config_defects lets amend through, while 'stack up' later refuses with 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline config-check names each defect' after /ok reported the config settled. Trigger: .ok-planner/config.json with "stack": {"start": "...", "tag_variable": "WEB_PORT"} and "ports": ["WEB_PORT"], or the retired object form holding WEB_PORT. Harm (A3): /ok refuses the owner's correct repair, or reports settled a config the stack tool refuses. Scope: caused (stackDefects and the stack entry in CONFIG_CHECK_KEYS are new). From report i6.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack:remove_docker (with ::docker_ids, ::docker_out, ::in_use). Where docker is on PATH but its daemon is not running (Docker Desktop installed and stopped), 'docker ps -a -q --filter label=ok.run-tag=<tag>' exits 1 with 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon ...', which DOCKER_ABSENT does not match and docker_ids does not pass absent_ok for, so DockerFailed is recorded as a refusal for each of the four DOCKER_STEPS (stack:575-586). Trigger: a run that makes no docker object, such as this project's dashboard drive, taken down while the daemon is stopped. down keeps the entry with four refusals and exits 1 ('the run ... is not all taken down', stack:779-781) after deleting the run folder; cleanup's in_use then returns 'docker could not list its containers' (stack:796-800) and leaves the entry, so every converge drive and confirm round names a failed stack down while the daemon stays stopped, and a ports-declaring project keeps each lease. The work item says down deletes the entry once every removal succeeds and a refusal is docker refusing a removal; an unreachable daemon refused no removal of an object this run made. Harm (A3): an operator script gives a wrong result and leaves state where later use fails, on a correctly configured machine. Scope: caused (scripts/stack is new). From report i7.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack:start_run (with ::take_down, ::stop_group). start_run spawns the holder (stack:699) and only then records its pid (stack:700, record_holder, a locked transaction). Trigger: an exception or interrupt after spawn_holder returns and before record_holder writes the pid, such as Ctrl-C during the lock wait or a failed registry write. The except BaseException path calls take_down(root, tag, holder) (stack:710-712); claim returns the entry as the registry holds it, holder None, and stop_group returns at 'pgid = entry.get("holder"); if pgid is None: return None' (stack:536-538) without signalling or waiting the passed child. settle deletes the entry (no refusals), and the holder process ('python -c import signal; signal.pause() ok-stack-hold <tag>') runs forever with no registry entry, so neither down nor cleanup can find it. Harm (A1): an interrupt between two steps of opening a run leaves a running process no complete run produces and nothing records, against decision run-artifacts-recorded-by-the-stack-tool ('Every process the start command leaves running belongs to the process group the tool started it in, which down stops'). Driven with DOCKER_HOST at a dead socket: unreached at up and down -> took down, exit 0, entry gone; reached at up, unreached at down -> four refusals, exit 1, entry kept, then settled once docker answered. Entries without the field (None) keep the old path. The catch returns a value the caller acts on and emits STACK.DOCKER.UNREACHED inside the except (trace attached); kind unique by rg. Considered: a start command that itself starts the daemon, then the daemon stopped before down, would skip removal of labelled objects; too contrived a trigger to count as a new harm here.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack:start_run (with ::take_down, ::stop_group). start_run spawns the holder (stack:699) and only then records its pid (stack:700, record_holder, a locked transaction). Trigger: an exception or interrupt after spawn_holder returns and before record_holder writes the pid, such as Ctrl-C during the lock wait or a failed registry write. The except BaseException path calls take_down(root, tag, holder) (stack:710-712); claim returns the entry as the registry holds it, holder None, and stop_group returns at 'pgid = entry.get("holder"); if pgid is None: return None' (stack:536-538) without signalling or waiting the passed child. settle deletes the entry (no refusals), and the holder process ('python -c import signal; signal.pause() ok-stack-hold <tag>') runs forever with no registry entry, so neither down nor cleanup can find it. Harm (A1): an interrupt between two steps of opening a run leaves a running process no complete run produces and nothing records, against decision run-artifacts-recorded-by-the-stack-tool ('Every process the start command leaves running belongs to the process group the tool started it in, which down stops'). Scope: caused (scripts/stack is new). From report i8.
note: stack:stop_group falls back to child.pid when the entry records no holder and take_down was passed the child; holder_is_ours confirms the mark and tag, SIGTERM to its group and child.wait reap it. Driven by exec-loading the script and replacing record_holder with one raising KeyboardInterrupt: the interrupt propagates, the registry is empty, no ok-stack-hold process remains. down and cleanup pass no child, so their path is unchanged.
